figures.title: Prithvi Narayan Shah
figures.description: King of Gorkha who began the unification of Nepal in the 18th century, shown in his best-known pose with one finger raised.

khukuri.label: Khukuri
khukuri.info: The curved knife of the Gorkhali soldier, carried tucked into the waist sash. It served as both an everyday tool and a weapon, and remains a national symbol of Nepal.

tarwar.label: Tarwar (Sword)
tarwar.info: A long curved sword held point-down in the left hand. Swords like this were carried by Gorkhali commanders during the unification campaigns.

dhal.label: Dhal (Shield)
dhal.info: A round shield, traditionally made of hide or metal with raised bosses, worn at the hip and used together with the sword.

shripech.label: Shripech (Crown)
shripech.info: The jewelled royal crown of the Shah kings, topped with a plume of bird-of-paradise feathers.

mala.label: Mala (Garland)
mala.info: A garland worn around the neck. Statues of Prithvi Narayan Shah are garlanded with marigolds on Prithvi Jayanti, the day that marks his birth.

patuka.label: Patuka (Waist Sash)
patuka.info: A long cloth wound around the waist over the robe. It holds the khukuri in place and supports the back.

jutta.label: Jutta (Shoes)
jutta.info: Leather shoes with upturned, pointed toes, a style worn at court in the period.

suruwal.label: Suruwal (Trousers)
suruwal.info: Close-fitting trousers worn under the robe, tight from the knee down to the ankle.

jama.label: Jama (Robe)
jama.info: A long-sleeved robe with a wide pleated skirt that falls to the knee, the formal dress of the court.

figures.title: Nepali Man in Daura Suruwal
figures.description: A man in Daura Suruwal with a Dhaka Topi, the traditional dress of Nepali men.

dhaka_topi.label: Dhaka Topi
dhaka_topi.info: A cap made from Dhaka, a hand-woven patterned cotton cloth. It is taller at the front than the back and is a symbol of Nepali identity.

jutta.label: Jutta (Shoes)
jutta.info: Plain leather shoes, the usual footwear with Daura Suruwal today.

daura.label: Daura (Shirt)
daura.info: A knee-length double-breasted shirt closed with eight ties instead of buttons. Its closed neck and five pleats carry traditional religious meanings.

suruwal.label: Suruwal (Trousers)
suruwal.info: Trousers that are loose at the top and narrow tightly towards the ankle.

coat.label: Coat
coat.info: A Western-style coat worn over the daura. It was added to the outfit in the 19th century and is now a standard part of formal dress.

figures.title: Nepali Woman in Kurtha Suruwal
figures.description: A woman in Kurtha Suruwal with a Saal, everyday traditional dress for Nepali women.

saal.label: Saal (Shawl)
saal.info: A long shawl draped over the shoulder. It is worn for warmth and modesty and is often the most decorated piece of the outfit.

suruwal.label: Suruwal (Trousers)
suruwal.info: Trousers worn under the kurtha, gathered or fitted closely at the ankle.

kurtha.label: Kurtha (Tunic)
kurtha.info: A long tunic that reaches the knee, with slits at the sides so the wearer can move freely. It is worn over the suruwal.

figures.title: Nepali Man with Istakot and Dhaka Topi
figures.description: A man in Daura Suruwal, wearing a patterned Istakot (waistcoat) and a Dhaka Topi.

dhaka_topi.label: Dhaka Topi
dhaka_topi.info: A cap cut from Dhaka, a hand-woven patterned cloth. It is taller at the front than at the back and is a symbol of Nepali identity.

istakot.label: Istakot (Waistcoat)
istakot.info: A sleeveless waistcoat worn over the daura. This one is cut from patterned Dhaka-style cloth, with the diamond motifs the fabric is known for.

shoes.label: Shoes
shoes.info: Plain black leather shoes, now the usual footwear with Daura Suruwal.

suruwal.label: Suruwal (Trousers)
suruwal.info: Trousers worn with the daura, traditionally loose at the top and narrowing towards the ankle. Here they are cut straight, with a band of the Dhaka pattern at each cuff.

daura.label: Daura (Shirt)
daura.info: A knee-length shirt with a crossed front that closes with ties at the side. It is worn over the suruwal and under the waistcoat.
